A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAKE benchmark and BIRD editing method. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison; relocated material and renumbered analyses can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original BAKE evaluations of BIRD and baseline editors on four LLMs, together with objective-weight sensitivity and answer-probability analyses (Tables 3–4, Section 6 and Appendix C).

after.justification: v2 reports original BAKE editing results and retains the sensitivity and answer-probability analyses, including the supplementary results for three LLMs (Table 3, Section 6 and Appendix D).

M1.justification: BIRD retains the same ROME-based rank-one update and four objectives for strengthening new facts and weakening old facts bidirectionally. The combined loss in v1 Section 6.1 matches v2 Section 5; the new schematic does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain BAKE-Q&J and BAKE-J with the same factual-editing tasks, relation categories and QA/judgment coverage. Table 2 retains 4,694 and 3,184 edits across 25 and 20 relations. The additional currency-template example does not establish expanded evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: FT, KN, MEND, MEMIT and ROME remain the comparators in both BAKE datasets. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the GPT-J portability/multi-hop comparison (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 4). Newly cited methods are not added to these evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported template-construction procedure from handwritten templates to ChatGPT-generated templates using gpt-3.5-turbo. v2 also drops probability-magnitude metrics while retaining the corresponding success-rate metrics; PS and NS are renamed GS and LS. These are revisions within the retained evaluation framework, without evidence establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The objective-weight sensitivity study and original-versus-desired answer-probability analyses are retained, including the appendix plots. v1 Figures 3–7 match v2 Figures 4–8. The added BIRD diagram is explanatory rather than a new ablation or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same significance annotations and t-test threshold of p < 0.05 in the main results. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or an additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 removes the secondary magnitude-result series EM, PM, NM, RQM and RJM. Among retained table entries, GPT-J's unedited BAKE-J Score changes from 0.00 to 24.44, and BIRD's LLaMA-2 BAKE-Q&J generalization score changes from 94.76 to 96.20. Other matched scores and experimental plots remain unchanged. These unexplained numerical revisions do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: The ROME mathematics, contextual-representation assumption and BIRD objectives remain unchanged. The full ROME exposition moves to Appendix A, while newly written indicator-function formulas restate existing score definitions. No new proof, theorem or substantive mathematical reasoning is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about BAKE, reversibility and BIRD's mitigation of the reversal curse remain. However, v2 omits the introduction's explicit claim that the method eliminates a training step and requires no extra training data, removing a limited claimed advantage.

C2.justification: The new limitations paragraph explicitly identifies non-autoregressive models as unexplored. v2 also removes v1 Section 5.3's explanation that larger models overcome the harder reverse judgments associated with BAKE-J relation categories. The limitation concerning poor reverse-QA performance was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a currency-template example but removes the BAKE repository address and the disclosure that the objective-weight study used only 300 examples. This omission does not establish a sample-size change. The EasyEdit setup, baseline access links and BIRD hyperparameter values remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Transformer-interpretability subsection and memory-based editing discussion, while adding citations including Cohen et al. (2023), Li et al. (2023), Gandikota et al. (2023), and Ma et al. (2024a,b). These update the background coverage; the central positioning against unidirectional editing and the claimed bidirectional novelty remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially condensed and reorganized. BIRD moves before the experiments, its results join the experimental section, and the full ROME exposition moves into an appendix. Related work is shortened, metric explanations are reorganized, and limitations and impact statements are added.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, and a new BIRD schematic becomes Figure 3. The separate BAKE-Q&J and BAKE-J results tables are consolidated into a side-by-side table with revised headers and fewer columns. Appendix tables and plots are relocated, while the experimental plot content is retained.

improvement.justification: The clearer organization, new schematic and explicit limitations are useful. However, v2 introduces a numerical inconsistency: Table 3 assigns unedited GPT-J a BAKE-J harmonic Score of 24.44 despite zero reversibility, where v1 reported 0.00. It also removes the 300-example sensitivity-study disclosure and BAKE repository address. These limited losses in numerical reliability and reproducibility outweigh the presentation benefits.
